feature: A placed picture keeps its own name
summary: Dropping a file in from the Finder or placing a capture from the Library now names the layer after the file instead of calling everything Pasted Image, so a stack of placed pictures reads at a glance in the Layers list.
setup: Photonz Dev with a document open. Steps 1, 2, 6 and 7 work in either release. Steps 3 to 5 need the Library, which is release Next with next-library on in the Experiments window.

try.do: Open any picture, then drag an image file in from the Finder and drop it on the canvas.
Look at the top row of the Layers list: it should read the file's name without its extension, not Pasted Image.
Choose View > Show Library, type screenshot in the search box and press Return to pick the top tile.
Click Place in Picture, or double click the tile.
Read the new row: a capture the app named itself arrives as its clock time, like Screenshot 16.22.12, not its whole file name.
Copy an image in another app, come back and press ⌘V: with no file behind it, that one still reads Pasted Image.
Double click any of those rows, rename it, then press ⌘Z: the name it arrived with comes back.

evaluate: Reading three or four placed pictures in the list, can you tell which is which without clicking any of them?
A capture arrives as Screenshot 16.22.12. Is the clock time the part you would recognise it by, or would you rather see the date?
The Library tile calls that same capture 9 hours ago while the layer calls it Screenshot 16.22.12. Does the mismatch bother you?
Pasted Image is still the name for a clipboard picture. Is that the right word for it, or would something like Image read better?
Placing the same capture twice gives you two rows with the identical name. Does that need a 2 on the end, or is it fine?
rough: Naming a placed capture after its full file name, which is literally what the task asked for, does not work: Screenshot 2026-09-02 at 16.22.12 measures about 220pt of text and the Layers panel is 220pt wide including thumbnails and buttons, so every capture would truncate to the identical Screenshot 2026-09-02 a... The layer keeps only the part that tells two captures apart, the clock time. A file a person named is untouched and keeps its whole name.
Nothing dedupes names: two copies of the same file give two identical rows. Renaming one is the only way to tell them apart.

The shortening only recognises the app's own two prefixes, Screenshot and Recording, followed by a real date. A capture from some other tool with its own timestamp format keeps its full name and will truncate.
Pasting a file copied in the Finder still reads Pasted Image, because the clipboard hands over pixels rather than the file.
Screenshots are real captures of the probe app, taken by Scripts/playtest/placed-image-name-walk.json (Screen Recording was granted).
